title: Rama Accepts Exile
text:
King Dasharatha of Ayodhya, growing old, decided to crown his eldest son Rama as heir. The city rejoiced. But his young queen Kaikeyi, stirred up by her maid Manthara, reminded the king of two boons he had promised her long ago when she saved his life in battle.

Now she named them: her own son Bharata must be crowned instead, and Rama must be sent into the forest for fourteen years. Dasharatha begged her to choose anything else, but he had given his word and could not take it back.

When Rama was summoned, he saw his father's grief and heard the demand from Kaikeyi. He did not argue or protest. He said he would go gladly so that his father would not break his promise. His wife Sita insisted on going with him, and his brother Lakshmana would not be left behind either. The three set out in bark clothing, while the people of Ayodhya followed weeping.

Soon after they left, Dasharatha died of grief. Bharata, returning home, refused the throne and went to the forest to beg Rama to come back. Rama still refused, so Bharata took his brother's sandals, set them on the throne, and ruled only as Rama's deputy until his return.
lesson: Keeping faith with family can cost a great deal. Honoring a commitment, even one you did not make, can hold a family together when everything else is pulling it apart.
people: Rama, Dasharatha, Kaikeyi, Sita, Lakshmana, Bharata
date: c. 5th century BC to 3rd century AD
